Consult Summary:
- Middle-aged male with history of hypertension and high cholesterol presented via telemedicine with acute central chest pressure (7/10) for a few hours with shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting), and left shoulder/arm pain; advised emergency ambulance transfer for suspected cardiac etiology.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Central chest discomfort described as pressure “like someone sitting on the chest.”
- Onset/duration: Began a couple of hours prior to consult; sudden onset.
- Severity: 7/10 at onset and unchanged at time of consult.
- Location/character: Mid-chest pressure/discomfort rather than sharp pain.
- Radiation: To left shoulder and arm; not to head; no further radiation reported.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Shortness of breath; light-headedness.
  - Nausea; no vomiting.
  - Exertional dyspnea noted recently with difficulty climbing stairs or walking uphill.
  - Reports calf pain and leg swelling with exertion.
  - No dysphagia or difficulty drinking.
  - No genitourinary or bowel issues reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not specified.
- Functional impact: Limiting daily activity to light movement around the house due to exertional symptoms.
- Timeline/activities at onset:
  - Patient initially reported onset while “digging in the garden.”
  - Later stated he was relaxing and watching TV with wife when symptoms occurred.
  - Conflict noted.
- Systems review pertinent negatives: No vomiting; no swallowing difficulty; no urinary/bowel problems.

Past Medical History:
- Hypertension (history noted; current management not documented).
- High cholesterol (history noted; current management not documented).

Medications:
- No current medications reported.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Tobacco: Smokes (quantity/frequency not documented).
- Living situation: Lives at home with wife.
- Physical activity: Gardening every other week; currently limiting activity due to exertional dyspnea.
- Alcohol/substance use: Not documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- 

Investigations:
- None documented during telemedicine consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute chest pressure with concerning features (SOB, light-headedness, left shoulder/arm pain, nausea) in patient with HTN and hyperlipidemia.
  - Concern for cardiac cause.
  - Plan:
    - Immediate ambulance activation for emergency evaluation at hospital.
    - Patient advised to remain calm, may sip water if needed.
    - Advised not to take any medications prior to paramedic arrival.
    - Paramedics to assess heart and breathing; monitoring and checks expected on arrival.
    - Anticipated rapid assessment by hospital consultant on arrival.
- Issue 2: Shortness of breath with exertional limitation; reports calf pain and leg swelling with exertion.
  - Plan:
    - Included in emergency evaluation; paramedics/hospital team to assess respiratory status and lower extremity symptoms.
- Issue 3: Hypertension and high cholesterol (no current medications reported).
  - Plan:
    - To be reviewed after acute event; clinician will book follow-up appointment post-hospital evaluation.

General Plan items:
- Doctor to remain available and arrange follow-up after hospital visit.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies not documented; medication reconciliation limited; vitals and physical exam not performed/documented; detailed smoking history (amount/duration) not obtained; family history not obtained.
- Internal conflicts: Inconsistent report of activity at symptom onset (gardening vs relaxing watching TV). Age stated as both 53 and 54 (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor interruptions/overlaps; some incomplete responses.
